disposition_reason: As, Cr, Cd, Pb and Hg were measured by INAA and ICP-AES in 7 rice and 12 dry pasta products bought in Arak, Iran; Table 2 prints mean ± SD of triplicates per product.

study.design: Pilot convenience market sample (19 retail products) with probabilistic cancer risk modelling and machine learning
study.origin: rice from Thailand, India, Pakistan and Iran; pasta from major Iranian manufacturers
study.market: 15 supermarkets and 10 local markets, Arak, Iran
study.method: INAA (MNSR reactor) and ICP-AES after closed-vessel microwave digestion (HNO3/H2O2); Hg by INAA only
study.qa: NIST SRM 1568b rice flour with each batch, recoveries 85-115%; method blanks and duplicates

unresolved: Accepted manuscript (Article in Press, unedited); values may change in the final version.
Many pasta values (Cd, Pb, Hg) and all rice Hg values are below the stated LODs of both methods; flagged per finding.
Which method (INAA or ICP-AES) produced each value is not stated.
Pasta type (spaghetti, penne, macaroni) is not given per product.
Arsenic is total arsenic; Cr is total chromium.

regulatory_or_exposure.what: ELCR from rice and pasta for consumption scenarios
regulatory_or_exposure.value: see Table 3; highest risk with long-term exposure

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Comparators cited: Codex As in polished rice 0.2 mg/kg; EU Hg in cereals 0.1 mg/kg (as stated by authors); Pb 0.2 mg/kg
regulatory_or_exposure.value: MF-3 Hg 0.502 mg/kg and MF-8 As 0.834 mg/kg exceed these; confirmed by reanalysis
